html:
The Battle of Jeddah was a siege that lasted through most of 1925. Ibn Saud, the ruler of Nejd, took the Red Sea port of Jeddah, now in Saudi Arabia, from King Ali of Hejaz. It ended the rule of the Hashemite family over the holy cities of Islam.

The Hashemite Hussein bin Ali, sharif of Mecca, had led the Arab Revolt and made himself king of Hejaz in 1916. In 1924, after Turkey abolished the caliphate, he claimed the title of caliph. Ibn Saud and his Ikhwan warriors, followers of the strict Wahhabi teaching, attacked. They took Taif, with a massacre, and then Mecca. Hussein gave up the throne to his son Ali, who fell back to Jeddah with a small army and a few aircraft. The Saudis ringed the walled town and waited. Britain stayed out. Medina gave in early in December 1925, and Jeddah's leading men surrendered the town soon after. Ali sailed away to exile in Iraq.

In January 1926 Ibn Saud was declared king of Hejaz. In 1932 he joined his lands as Saudi Arabia, which has held Mecca and Medina ever since. The Hashemites kept only Iraq, until 1958, and Jordan.
